world.h: Trump rules out immediate attack on Iran
world.b: Al Jazeera's live coverage: Trump rules out an immediate attack on Iran as Qatari mediators visit Tehran.
world.title: Trump rules out immediate attack on Iran; Qatar mediators in Tehran

national.h: Texas cop's ICE work tore his town apart
national.b: ProPublica profiles Jaron Alexander of Ingram, Texas, one of more than 29,000 local officers on the front lines of the Trump administration's deportation campaign.
national.title: The Small-Town Cop Who Helped ICE Deport His Neighbors

national.h: N.Y. woman says she didn't know she wasn't a citizen
national.b: A 66-year-old Syracuse woman faces a federal charge of voting by an alien. She says she only learned of her German birth certificate while searching for her biological mother.

national.h: U.S. birth rate drops to record low
national.b: The U.S. birth rate has fallen to a record low, though older women are having more babies, NPR reports.

national.h: Severe flooding hits Four Corners region
national.b: Historic flooding along the San Juan River forced evacuations and rooftop rescues, with more rain expected through the weekend.

politics.h: Obama slams Trump's 'cruelty and corruption' in Ohio
politics.b: At a rally for Ohio Democrats, Barack Obama said Trump started 'an unnecessary war that nobody asked for' and urged voters to reject the Republican administration.

politics.h: Trump casts his midterm ballot early in Florida
politics.b: Trump voted early in person in Florida and said he voted the party line. He again defended Vivek Ramaswamy's ad featuring Amy Acton's estranged mother.

politics.h: US cuts staff at 4 Mideast embassies over Iran threats
politics.b: The U.S. is reducing staffing at four Middle East embassies after a memo warned Iranian plotting against U.S. citizens had reached advanced stages.

politics.h: Pentagon calls Confucius Institutes a security threat
politics.b: Defense Secretary Hegseth said the Pentagon added the Chinese-backed Confucius Institutes to its list of institutions that threaten national security.

politics.h: DOJ orders California counties to verify ballots
politics.b: Federal prosecutors sent letters to county registrars across California demanding they set aside and verify ballots the Justice Department says may belong to noncitizens, within 48 hours.
politics.title: DOJ orders some California counties to verify ballots in 48 hours

international.h: Machado returns to Venezuela after exile
international.b: Opposition leader María Corina Machado returned to Venezuela after months in exile, writing 'I am here. With you.' Edmundo González said he would join her soon.
international.title: Venezuela's opposition leader Machado returns after months in exile

international.h: Burnham open to EU freedom of movement talks
international.b: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham told The Sunday Times he wants to discuss a return to EU freedom of movement as he rethinks ties with Brussels.
international.title: UK PM Burnham says he wants to discuss a return to EU freedom of movement

international.h: Brazil votes in tight Lula-Bolsonaro run-off
international.b: Al Jazeera's live coverage: Lula and Bolsonaro face off in Brazil's presidential run-off in a tight race.
international.title: Voters take to the polls in Brazil’s presidential elections

international.h: Algeria's senate approves troops for Niger
international.b: Algeria's upper house approved a troop deployment to Niger in an emergency session. If the lower house agrees, it would be Algeria's first mission abroad since 1973.
international.title: Algerian parliament’s upper house approves troop deployment to Niger

international.h: Israeli troops turn Hebron homes into posts
international.b: Israeli forces took over homes in southern Hebron as barracks and observation posts amid a lockdown and hundreds of raids since Friday's attack, Wafa reported.
international.title: Israeli forces turn Hebron homes into military posts amid lockdown

international.h: Iran blames US for deal failure, urges new try
international.b: President Pezeshkian blamed the US for the failed deal but said both sides should return and conclude it, amid fears military action could resume as soon as this weekend.

international.h: Thousands of Israelis rally against Netanyahu
international.b: Thousands rallied days before Israel's election at a protest organised by the October Council, founded by families of captives taken to Gaza, demanding accountability for the failure to prevent the Hamas attack.

international.h: About 25,000 rally in Madrid for state pensions
international.b: Protesters from across Spain marched in Madrid in support of the state pension scheme ahead of next month's general election, citing pressure from an ageing population and stagnant wages.

international.h: Soldiers deploy as protesters rally in Milan
international.b: Hundreds of soldiers spread across Milan and luxury boutiques were boarded up as protesters marched, a week after demonstrations spiralled into clashes and looting.
Defence Minister Yevhenii Khmara said Starlink and Starshield connections are stable again, crediting talks with Washington and Zelenskyy's diplomacy, as attacks continue in Russia and Ukraine.

international.h: Fire engulfs Hitler's Eagle's Nest; suspect held
international.b: About 200 firefighters battled an overnight blaze at the Kehlsteinhaus in Bavaria. No injuries were reported, and police are examining whether a suspicious person taken into custody was involved.

international.h: Kim Jong Un visits China via new bridge
international.b: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un crossed into China over the newly opened border bridge and met Chinese Premier Li Qiang, a day before the anniversary of China joining the Korean War.

international.h: Rubio urges Cubans to partner with CIA
international.b: Secretary of State Marco Rubio called on Cubans to partner with the CIA 'to create positive change,' after months of US officials hinting at intervention in Cuba.

international.h: Israeli raids hit 15 West Bank towns
international.b: Israeli forces raided at least 15 towns in the northern West Bank, including Nablus, Jenin, Tubas and Qalqilya, detaining dozens of Palestinians after a Hebron attack killed two soldiers.

international.h: Argentine judge drops Milei crypto probe
international.b: Judge Marcelo Martinez de Giorgi ended an inquiry into President Milei's role in the launch of the $Libra token, ruling the events were not a criminal offence.

international.h: Thousands mourn victims of Jordan church attack
international.b: Nine people were killed and dozens wounded in the rare attack on Jordan's Christian minority, prompting three days of national mourning.
international.title: Thousands mourn victims of deadly Jordan church attack

international.h: Police clear Lisbon housing protest camp, arrest 25
international.b: Portuguese police moved in on the camp in Rossio Square early Sunday, where protesters had pitched more than 100 tents, arresting 25.
international.title: Portuguese police clear Lisbon housing protest camp, arrest 25

international.h: Lula, Bolsonaro spar over economy before run-off
international.b: In a debate two days before Brazil's run-off, the candidates clashed over the economy, infrastructure and regional development, with Lula attacking his rival's 'chainsaw' spending plan.

international.h: Taiz hospital warns of collapse within days
international.b: A dialysis centre treating 270 patients in Yemen's government-held city of Taiz says medical supplies and fuel are critically low under the renewed Houthi siege.

sports.b: Baylor fired Dave Aranda, who won the 2021 Big 12 title but posted four losing records in six full seasons.
sports.title: Baylor fires Dave Aranda: Lincoln Riley, Spencer Danielson among candidates to replace 7th-year coach

sports.h: Brewers rally past Rays 5-4 in World Series
sports.b: The Rays scored four runs in the first inning, but Milwaukee chipped away and took the lead in the bottom of the seventh. The Brewers are 9-1 this postseason.

sports.h: Upsets throw Big 12 playoff picture into chaos
sports.b: Cincinnati snapped Texas Tech's nine-game Big 12 winning streak and Scott Frost's Knights held off BYU, a week after the Cougars rose to No. 2.

sports.h: NC State fires coach Dave Doeren
sports.b: NC State fired Dave Doeren in his 14th season after a loss to Stanford dropped the Wolfpack to 3-4.

sports.h: WNBA Finals Game 6 venue up in the air
sports.b: Game 6 of the Dream-Valkyries Finals is listed as TBD because the Hawks are scheduled to host the Cavaliers at State Farm Arena the same night.

sports.h: Petr Yan outduels Dvalishvili to keep UFC title
sports.b: Petr Yan retained his bantamweight title against Merab Dvalishvili at UFC 333 in a Fight of the Year contender.
Milwaukee beat the Rays 3-2 in Game 1 at American Family Field after a week off. Christian Yelich tripled home Jackson Chourio in a two-run first inning.

sports.h: Bears flagged for rare illegal forward handing
sports.b: The Bears became the first team in 16 years to be called for illegal forward handing, on a trick play against the Patriots that lost five yards.

sports.h: Utah DT Jamal Wallace suspended after arrest
sports.b: Utah suspended Wallace indefinitely after his arrest on suspicion of distributing intimate images. A woman also accused him of rape, an affidavit shows.

local.h: Ex-NYPD detective in GWB killing out on bail
local.b: Victor Romero, 62, charged with manslaughter in the shooting death of ConEd worker Koran Irvine on the George Washington Bridge, posted $1 million bail.
local.title: Retired NYPD detective charged in George Washington Bridge killing out on $1M bail

local.h: Rural hospital cuts become NY governor race issue
local.b: Candidates for governor are trading blame as rural hospitals face cuts, including Albany Med's plan to curtail services at Columbia Memorial Health in Hudson.
local.title: Cuts to rural healthcare become key issue for upstate votes in race for NY governor

local.h: NY Archdiocese agrees to pay $800M to abuse survivors
local.b: The Archdiocese of New York agreed to pay $800 million to 1,300 people who say they were sexually abused by clergy, lay leaders and teachers. The deal is set to be signed the first week of November.

local.h: Chinatown residents sue over jail night work
local.b: Residents and advocacy groups sued the city over plans to allow after-hours construction on the new Chinatown jail, citing sleep disruption and dust.
local.title: Chinatown residents file lawsuit against after-hours construction on new 'mega jail'

local.h: NYPD officer shoots woman with knife in Queens
local.b: An officer shot and wounded a woman who approached police with a knife during a home invasion and stabbing call on 149th Street Friday night. She is in stable condition.
local.title: NYPD: Officer shot, injured knife-wielding woman during ‘chaotic’ night at Queens home

localgood.b: Suicide deaths in New York City fell from a peak of 601 in 2022 to 535 in 2024, health department data shows, though inequities persist across groups.
localgood.title: Suicides decline in NYC, but inequities persist across groups
